nodes.title: Reference import boundary
nodes.question: Should automatic reference inclusion allow linked regular files anywhere within the same source repository at its recorded revision, including shared documents outside a skill folder, while refusing links that escape that repository or require guessing another source?
nodes.agentRecommendationSummary: Yes. Use the recorded source repository as the boundary.
nodes.agentRecommendation: Follow links within that saved version of the source project. Keep the existing file-size and file-type limits. If a link leaves the project or exceeds a limit, explain the problem and stop instead of installing an incomplete skill.

help.sourceQuestion: Should automatic reference inclusion allow linked regular files anywhere within the same source repository at its recorded revision, including shared documents outside a skill folder, while refusing links that escape that repository or require guessing another source?
help.sourceRecommendation:
Yes. Use the recorded source repository as the boundary.

Follow links within that saved version of the source project. Keep the existing file-size and file-type limits. If a link leaves the project or exceeds a limit, explain the problem and stop instead of installing an incomplete skill.

eli15.title: How far should we follow a skill’s links?
paragraphs: Imagine installing a skill that tells an AI how to review your work. It links to a checklist stored elsewhere in the same project.

We could bring that checklist along automatically. But if a link points outside the project, we would stop and explain what is missing. We would use the saved version of the project, so the files all match.
eli15.decision: Should we include linked files from anywhere in that same project, or keep them inside the skill’s own folder?
eli15.limits: This does not mean copying every file. We only follow links. Existing file-size and file-type limits still apply; an unsupported link stops the import.

eli18.title: Choose the boundary for following references
paragraphs: A repository is the source project. A recorded revision is a saved version of that project. A skill can link to a document outside its own folder but still inside that repository.

The proposal is to follow those links, and any further links, within the same recorded revision. This brings shared documents with the skill while keeping the imported files consistent. A narrower alternative allows only the skill’s own folder, which can leave shared documents unavailable.
eli18.decision: May imports follow references across the saved repository, while stopping at links that leave it?
eli18.limits: Existing import size and file-type limits still apply. A link outside the repository, an unsupported file, or an exceeded limit stops the import with an explanation. The importer does not guess another source or install a partial result.

walkthrough.title: Illustrative example: installing a review skill

steps.title: You install a code-review skill
paragraphs: The skill includes instructions for reviewing code. Those instructions refer to a shared checklist. To use the skill fully, the AI needs both files.

items.label: docs/review-checklist.md
items.detail: A linked checklist outside the skill folder

steps.title: The checklist is in the same project
paragraphs: With the proposed boundary, the importer includes the checklist even though it is outside the skill’s folder. Both files come from the same saved project version.

visual.title: Same project: include the linked document
visual.caption: Only linked files are included. Unrelated files stay behind.

steps.title: Another link leaves the project
paragraphs: Now imagine the checklist links to a policy in a different project. The importer stops and explains which link caused the problem. It does not guess where to fetch that policy or install an incomplete skill.

visual.title: Outside the project: stop the import
visual.caption: The skill is not installed until the unsupported reference is resolved.

steps.title: Your choice is where to draw the boundary
paragraphs: The whole saved project lets skills reuse shared documents. The skill folder alone is narrower, but would refuse the checklist in this example.
Either way, file-size and file-type limits still apply. The question asks whether the whole saved project is the right boundary.

nodes.title: Explain import failures
nodes.question: Should a failed import show which link caused the problem?
nodes.agentRecommendation: Show the source file and the unsupported link so the author knows what to fix.

help.sourceQuestion: Should a failed import show which link caused the problem?
help.sourceRecommendation:
Yes.

Show the source file and the unsupported link so the author knows what to fix.

eli15.title: Tell me which link needs fixing
paragraphs: Imagine adding a skill that points to a checklist, but the checklist is missing. The import stops. A message could tell you which file contains the broken link and where that link tried to go.
eli15.decision: Should the error message point out the exact link, so you know what to fix?

eli18.title: Identify the reference that failed
paragraphs: An import can fail when a file references a document that cannot be included. Showing the source file and referenced target makes the problem easier to trace than a generic “Import failed” message.
eli18.decision: Should a failed import identify the link that caused it?
eli18.limits: This choice concerns the error message. It does not change which files the importer permits or authorize installing an incomplete result.

steps.title: You try to install a review skill
paragraphs: The skill points to docs/checklist.md. Imagine that file is missing. The importer stops.

steps.title: Compare the two messages
paragraphs: A generic message says “Import failed.” You still have to find the problem.
A specific message says “skills/review/SKILL.md links to docs/checklist.md, which could not be found.” Now you know which link to check.

steps.title: Choose how much the message tells you
paragraphs: The question asks whether to identify that failed link. It does not change the import boundary or install the skill for you.
